item.title: Fulbright-Iméra Mediterranean Studies Award 2027-2028 (Aix-Marseille, US Faculty)
item.description:
Organisation: Iméra – Aix Marseille Université, in partnership with the Fulbright Commission

Location: Aix-Marseille, France (campus residency)

Award: €2,400 (~USD 2,600) monthly stipend; fully covered accommodation (valued USD 788–1,966/month); €1,200 (~USD 1,300) travel allowance. No application fee.

Duration: 5 or 10 months (September 2027 – June 2028, flexible start/end dates).

Deadline: 15 Sep 2026

The Fulbright-Iméra Mediterranean Studies Award supports US faculty to conduct research at the Iméra Institute for Advanced Study at Aix Marseille Université. ELIGIBILITY: mid-career, senior, or community college faculty affiliated with a US institution of higher education; US citizens residing outside France (permanent residents of France are ineligible); any discipline relating to Mediterranean studies; English sufficient (French desirable). 1 or 2 grants awarded. PROVIDED: €2,400/month stipend; fully equipped apartment with linens; office in co-working space; visa fees waived; academic event organisation expenses covered; school placement assistance for dependents. DURATION: 5 or 10 months (September 2027 – June 2028, flexible). DEADLINE: 15 September 2026. Apply via the Fulbright Scholar Program at https://fulbrightscholars.org/award/fulbright-imera-mediterranean-studies-award-aix-marseille-university.

item.title: American Academy in Berlin: Berlin Prize Fellowship 2027-28
item.description:
Organisation: American Academy in Berlin

Location: Berlin, Germany, at the Hans Arnhold Center. RESTRICTED: fellowships are open only to citizens and permanent residents of the United States.

Award: Monthly stipend of USD 5,000, plus roundtrip airfare, accommodation at or near the Hans Arnhold Center, partial board, in-house library services and professional networking opportunities. Roughly two dozen fellowships awarded each year. No application fee.

Duration: One full academic semester (about 4 months). Fall runs mid-August to mid-December; spring runs late January to late May.

Deadline: 25 Sep 2026

The American Academy in Berlin is an independent, nonprofit institute for advanced study in the arts, humanities, social sciences, law, journalism and public policy, whose primary mission is to strengthen the cultural and intellectual ties between the United States and Germany. Each year, after a rigorous selection process, the Academy awards roughly two dozen semester-long Berlin Prize fellowships to individuals who demonstrate excellence in their fields. DISCIPLINES: applications are welcome across the humanities, social sciences, law, journalism and various areas of public policy. The Academy generally encourages projects addressing pressing issues of the day, specifically naming democracy, security, technology and society (especially AI), energy including climate, and global order. Dedicated fellowships also support projects in Jewish studies, German studies, and public health and biotechnology. Project proposals need not focus on Germany, but candidates should explain how a residency in Berlin would enhance their work. NOT ACCEPTED: proposals in mathematics or the natural sciences. NOTE FOR ARTISTS: visual artists and composers are invited through separate, nomination-based competitions, so there is no open application route for them here. ELIGIBILITY: fellowships are restricted to citizens and permanent residents of the United States. Both emerging and established figures are eligible. PhD holders qualify as emerging scholars with a strong record of peer-reviewed work beyond the dissertation; candidates in non-academic fields such as journalism, filmmaking and policy need a significant record of publication or production; fiction and nonfiction writers must have published at least one book with a reputable press. WHAT FELLOWS DO: fellows present their work to audiences in and around Berlin through lectures, readings, public discussions, performances and film screenings, and should be willing to engage with relevant German institutions, organizations and the media; these activities are integral to the Academy's mission of fostering transatlantic dialogue. APPLICATION MATERIALS: a project proposal of 1,500 to 1,750 words plus a one-page bibliography; a curriculum vitae of up to 10 pages; two writing samples totalling no more than 60 pages; and three letters of recommendation, which are due 2 October 2026. DEADLINE: Friday 25 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Eastern Time (18:00 Central European Time). TIMELINE: all candidates are notified of the competition outcome by email in late March 2027; the 2027-28 Berlin Prize recipients are announced in May 2027.

Open call details

item.title: Earth Partner Prize 2026 (climate and ecological justice, ages 14 to 30)
item.description:
Organisation: Earth Partner, with the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and Re:wild

Location: Worldwide, any nationality. Entrants must be aged 14 to 30 at the time of submission; under-18s need parental consent.

Award: First prize USD 10,000; two runner-up awards of USD 5,000; five finalist awards of USD 2,000; plus one Impact Award and twenty honourable mentions. Free to enter.

Duration: Deadline 7 October 2026, 21:59. Timed to feed into the UN climate conference (COP) in November 2026.

Deadline: 07 Oct 2026

The Earth Partner Prize is a global open call for young creatives making work about climate action and ecological justice, run by Earth Partner with the Global Environment Facility and Re:wild, and timed to amplify youth voices ahead of the UN climate conference in November 2026. IT IS NOT A PHOTOGRAPHY PRIZE: the call takes work across disciplines, and the organisers explicitly list photography projects, docu-style and experimental film, performance art, app development, spoken word, musical compositions, dance, fashion design, new media and social media projects. PRIZES: USD 10,000 for first prize, USD 5,000 each for two runners-up, USD 2,000 each for five finalists, plus an Impact Award and twenty honourable mentions. ELIGIBILITY: aged 14 to 30 at the time of submission, any nationality, race, gender or faith; applicants under 18 need parental consent. SUBMISSION NOTES: entry is free, and entrants are asked to disclose any use of AI tools and to mention prior awards or press coverage in the project description. Submissions are handled on Picter; deadline 7 October 2026 at 21:59.

Open call details

item.title: Jamverse Jam (Protocolized worldbuilding contest)
item.description:
Organisation: Protocolized (Summer of Protocols)

Location: Online / Worldwide

Award: One USD 1,000 grand prize plus at least 10 additional USD 200 prizes; winning artifacts are published on the Jamverse website. No entry fee.

Duration: One-off contest; submit up to three artifacts by 31 July 2026

Deadline: Closed 31 Jul 2026

Protocolized's fourth contest invites artists and writers (storytellers, poets, comic artists) to build, extend, and connect the Jamverse, a shared near-future science fiction universe of four intersecting story cycles (The Stockton Chronicles, Legends and Ledgers, UET-Trainverse, and Zoothesia). ELIGIBILITY: open to anyone; you may submit up to three in-universe worldbuilding artifacts, and the same creator can win multiple prizes. REQUIREMENTS: each artifact must be under 1,000 words (200-700 is the sweet spot) or a visual equivalent (comic panel, poster, advertisement, etc.) and must include at least one element drawn from one of the four sub-world 'toy boxes', a surprising 'traffic jam' (an emergent, ah-ha consequence of a technology or protocol), and a relation to the theme of Stigmergy (indirect coordination through modifying a shared environment). Artifact types can include comic panels, job postings, poems, forum threads, historic documents, or encyclopedia entries. APPLY: submit each artifact as a public Google Doc via the contest form, including the artifact, a one-paragraph explanation of the worlds/toy-box components used and how the piece relates to stigmergy and explores a traffic jam, and, if AI was used, documentation of your AI/LLM protocol. PRIZES: one USD 1,000 grand prize and at least 10 USD 200 prizes, all published on the Jamverse website. DEADLINE: 31 July 2026. Contest rules, the current Jamverse stories, and starter materials are on the Jamverse website.

Open call details

item.title: SIAP: Major Individual Artists Award 2026/27 (Arts Council NI)
item.description:
Organisation: Arts Council of Northern Ireland

Location: Northern Ireland, United Kingdom. Applicants must be based in Northern Ireland.

Award: Up to GBP 15,000 per award; four awards available in 2026/27. Funded through the National Lottery Support for Individual Artists Programme (SIAP).

Duration: Supports specific projects, specialised research, personal artistic development and materials/equipment. Activity duration not specified.

Deadline: Closed 20 Jul 2026

The Major Individual Artists award, part of Arts Council NI's National Lottery Support for Individual Artists Programme (SIAP), funds extended or ambitious work by established artists, covering specific projects, specialised research, personal artistic development, and materials/equipment. AMOUNT: four awards of up to GBP 15,000 each in 2026/27. ELIGIBILITY: established artists across all disciplines with national/international recognition who have not previously received a major award; academics and postgraduate artists are eligible if the project costs do not relate to their institutional work or studies. Applicants must contact the relevant artform officer before submission (by 10 July 2026); applications without this prior contact are ineligible. No application fee. The online application system closes precisely at the deadline and applicants must receive a confirmation email to verify successful submission. Deadline: Monday 20 July 2026, 12:00 noon.

item.title: PLAYA Art/Sci Awarded Residency 2027
item.description:
Organisation: PLAYA

Location: Summer Lake, Lake County, Oregon, USA

Award: Awarded residency providing free lodging in a private cabin with kitchen and bathroom plus one weekly group meal. Residents cover their own travel, groceries, and materials. No cash stipend. USD 40 application fee (waivers granted on request by June 28, 2026)

Duration: 11 to 25 nights depending on session

Deadline: Closed 30 Jun 2026

PLAYA's Art/Sci Awarded Residency brings together artists and scientists for immersive, interdisciplinary inquiry at a rural retreat near Summer Lake in Lake County, Oregon. The 2027 cycle offers four session options ranging from 11 to 25 nights between January and November 2027. Awarded residents receive free lodging in a private cabin with kitchen and bathroom plus one weekly group meal, while covering their own travel, food, and materials. Both established and emerging practitioners in any media may apply, including naturalists, biologists, sound artists, new media artists, writers, performers, and interdisciplinary creators, and all applicants must be at least 18 years old. Applications are submitted through SlideRoom and require work samples and two references. There is a USD 40 application fee, though PLAYA states all fee waiver requests will be granted if submitted by June 28, 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Manuel António da Mota Prize – 17th Edition (2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Fundação Manuel António da Mota (FMAM)

Location: Portugal. Open to private social solidarity institutions and other non-profit entities working in eligible areas.

Award: Total prize fund. The winning application receives a cash prize of EUR 50,000. Second and third place receive EUR 25,000 and EUR 10,000 respectively. The remaining 7 applications (honourable mentions) each receive a cash prize of EUR 5,000.

Duration: One-off award.

Deadline: Closed 30 Jun 2026

In its 17th edition in 2026, under the motto 'Always in Solidarity,' the Manuel António da Mota Prize recognizes institutions that excel in the fight against poverty and social exclusion; the reception and integration of migrants and refugees; the development of rural areas and territorial cohesion; health; education; employment; family support; innovation and social entrepreneurship; inclusion and digital and technological transition; and climate transition. AWARDS: the winning application receives a cash prize of EUR 50,000; second and third place receive EUR 25,000 and EUR 10,000 respectively; the remaining seven applications (honourable mentions) each receive EUR 5,000. The prize is run by the Fundação Manuel António da Mota. Applications are open until 30 June 2026. See the foundation's current-edition page for full rules and eligibility.

Open call details

item.title: Mi-Hy: MudTronics Collaborative Competition 2026 (Bio, Tech, Art/Design)
item.description:
Organisation: Mi-Hy (with Empower / Universite Paris-Saclay)

Location: Online programme June-September 2026; in-person finals at Empower Universite Paris-Saclay, France (22-24 September 2026)

Award: Starter kit of essential materials for building microbial fuel cells (including carbon veil and membranes); online workshops with Mi-Hy scientists and regular feedback rounds; travel support to the in-person finals at Empower Universite Paris-Saclay (22-24 September 2026) for around 10 selected projects. No application fee.

Duration: Online programme runs June - September 2026; in-person finals 22-24 September 2026

Deadline: Closed 06 Jun 2026

MudTronics is a collaborative competition bringing together bio, tech, and art/design to explore microbial fuel cells: turning mud, wastewater and microbes into power, building prototypes that are playful, critical, and ecologically grounded. AIMS: inspire and connect local makers, artists, scientists, and technologists; develop new approaches for communication, sensing and ecological solutions; support team-based design and building of microbially-powered applications; empower knowledge transfer, local communities, and long-term collaborations; explore how a waste-driven low-power source can shape IOT, biorobotics, agriculture, and other spheres. PROGRAMME: selected proposals receive starter kits with essential materials (carbon veil, membranes) in June; teams work independently through July-August, supported by online workshops with Mi-Hy scientists and regular feedback rounds; around 10 projects are then invited (with travel support) to the in-person finals at Empower Universite Paris-Saclay in France (22-24 September 2026) for collaboration, feedback, and reflection with each other, local communities, and the more-than-human environments that make microbial power possible. OPEN FOR: organisations and collectives; artists and researchers/critics; cross-disciplinary, digital/new-media practitioners. DEADLINE: 6 June 2026. APPLY via the Mi-Hy MudTronics page.

Open call details

item.title: Ars Electronica: State of the ART(ist) 2026 (Linz)
item.description:
Organisation: Ars Electronica, in cooperation with the Austrian Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs

Location: Linz, Austria (international open call; project presented at the Ars Electronica Festival)

Award: Main Prize EUR 6,000 plus Award of Distinction EUR 4,000. Both selected projects are presented at the Ars Electronica Festival (9 to 13 September 2026, Linz). No application fee.

Duration: One-off prize plus festival presentation

Deadline: Closed 24 May 2026

International open call by Ars Electronica for artists whose livelihoods and working conditions are severely affected by political repression, war, restrictions on freedom of expression, environmental crises, or economic and systemic exploitation. ELIGIBILITY: individual artists and collectives working in artistic, cultural, social, academic, activist or interdisciplinary fields; proof of risk or instability is a baseline eligibility requirement and projects are then evaluated on artistic quality.

item.title: 2027 Elevate Prize
item.description:
Organisation: Elevate Prize Foundation

Location: Worldwide (US 501(c)(3) or international equivalent)

Award: $300,000 unrestricted ($250,000 to organisation + $50,000 to the individual)

Duration: 2-year tailored programme + global community

Deadline: Closed 08 May 2026

Nomination-based prize for nonprofit leaders driving meaningful change. Each winner receives $300,000 in unrestricted funding plus a two-year tailored programme with visibility, scaling support and a global community. Eligibility: 18+, serving as Executive Director, CEO, Founder or equivalent of a registered nonprofit (US 501(c)(3) or international equivalent) able to receive philanthropic funds. Ideally for organisations with annual budgets between $2M and $10M (others may be considered based on readiness and impact opportunity).
